name: The Sumerian Eleven
note: The same economy fifteen hundred years earlier, and it is not a reskin — the graph is a different SHAPE. Nisaba holds grain and writing together, so two Hellenic nodes collapse into one and the record arrives at the same moment as the surplus rather than after the market. Authority splits the other way: An is rank with nothing to act on and Enlil is the half that does something, so where the Hellenic board has one Zeus this one has a figurehead and an executive, and only the second is downstream of anything. Eleven nodes, not twelve, and the count is the finding. Mappings follow sumer.html where that page states them; where it does not, the choice is marked in the why and is meant to be argued with — that is what an editable template is for.

sectors.name: Inanna
sectors.why: Wanting, and she is also the planet you are standing on — Inanna is Venus, and was before anybody called it that in Latin. Desire is a root here for the same reason it is a root anywhere: nobody farms without wanting something.

sectors.name: Enki
sectors.why: The fresh water under everything, and the keeper of the me — the itemised list of the components of civilisation. Water first, because nothing sites itself before somebody has decided where the water is.

sectors.name: Ninhursag
sectors.why: The foothills and the ground itself. Shelter is a root because everything else needs an address, and this roster puts that in the earth rather than in a hearth.

sectors.name: Ninshubur
sectors.why: Inanna's messenger, and the one sent between powers when something has to move that nobody owns. Placed on the commons because that is the sector whose health cannot be read off its own activity — her activity is that nothing has gone wrong yet.

sectors.name: Nisaba
sectors.why: Grain AND writing, in one hand, which is the whole difference between this board and the Hellenic one. Two nodes there, one here — and the consequence is that the record does not have to wait for a market, because the person counting the barley is already the person who writes.

sectors.name: Ninagal
sectors.why: Enki's smith. Downstream of the surplus for the same reason every forge is: the hands at the fire are hands not growing food, and somebody else grew it.

sectors.name: The me
sectors.why: Enki's decrees — a list, itemised, of the components of civilisation, and Inanna takes them from him to Uruk. Craft as a transferable inventory rather than as a talent, which is a genuinely different theory of skill from Athena's and is why it gets its own node.

sectors.name: Ninurta
sectors.why: Plough and war in one figure, which is more honest than separating them. Downstream of the surplus, because force needs something worth taking before it is worth budgeting for.

sectors.name: The errand
sectors.why: Ninshubur again, in her other function: the one sent between powers. Needs two producers with different surpluses — with one producer there is no market, only a stall. MARKED: sumer.html does not assign trade explicitly and this is the defensible reading, not a stated one.

sectors.name: Utu
sectors.why: The sun, who sees everything, and therefore justice and the oath. He needs the record and the record is Nisaba — but Nisaba is already running by the time anybody has eaten, so on this board the oath is available far earlier than it is on the Hellenic one. That is the shape change, stated as a dependency.

sectors.name: An · Enlil
sectors.why: One node holding a split. An is the sky and the highest authority and does essentially nothing; Enlil is the half that acts, and only that half is downstream of anything. Where the Hellenic board needs a rule AND a record before authority can adjudicate, this one needs the oath alone — because the record came with the grain.
